name: Kana
note: Syllabary: 46 basic hiragana, each with a katakana counterpart.

section_notes.Small kana: Not shapes of their own. JSL signs the base kana and draws the hand back toward the signer, so each is its base hand with that arrow under it.
section_notes.Voiced kana: Not shapes of their own. JSL signs the base kana and moves the hand, sideways for the dakuten and upward for the handakuten, so each is its base hand with that arrow under it.

letters.name: shi
letters.notes: /ɕi/, not /si/ — the s row is irregular here.

letters.name: ha
letters.notes: Said /wa/ when it marks the topic of a sentence, /ha/ otherwise.

letters.name: fu
letters.notes: /ɸɯ/, closer to a soft blown f than an English h or f.

letters.name: he
letters.notes: Said /e/ when it marks direction, /he/ otherwise.

letters.name: wo
letters.example_gloss: object particle, never starts a word
letters.notes: Only used to mark the object, and pronounced the same as お.

letters.name: n
letters.example_gloss: mandarin — ん never starts a word
letters.notes: Takes its place from what follows: /m/ before p b m, /ŋ/ before k g, /n/ elsewhere.

letters.notes: Doubles the consonant that follows; it is never read on its own.

letters.name: chouonpu
letters.notes: Lengthens the vowel before it, in katakana. In JSL it is not spelled either: the hand that made the kana before it moves downward, and straight down, or it reads as の. Some teaching draws the ー stroke in the air instead, so this is the commoner of two conventions rather than the only one.

movement.name: chōonpu
movement.label: ー
movement.description: the hand already made moves downward

letters.name: dakuten
letters.notes: Voices the kana it sits on: ka becomes ga, sa becomes za, ta becomes da, ha becomes ba. In JSL the mark is not spelled: the base kana is signed and the hand moves to the side.

movement.name: dakuten
movement.description: the hand moves to the side

letters.name: handakuten
letters.notes: Turns the ha row into pa. In JSL the base kana is signed and the hand moves upward.

movement.name: handakuten
movement.description: the hand moves upward
